sources.title: "Har Gobind Khorana: The chemist who cracked DNA's code..." (The Conversation) -- documents his childhood poverty and early education
"Har Gobind Khorana, the Modest Professor" (The Wire Science) -- documents his post-PhD unemployment, self-funded postdoc, and Nobel-lecture framing
MIT School of Science's account of Khorana's career across UBC, Wisconsin, and MIT

persistence.rationale: Two independent documented instances: overcame post-PhD unemployment after returning to newly independent India in 1949 by leveraging his scientific network to secure a position at Alexander Todd's laboratory in the UK; and self-funded an additional postdoctoral position under Vladimir Prelog from his own savings rather than stopping his training when no external funding was available.

achievement_drive.rationale: A sustained, escalating institutional career trajectory (University of British Columbia, then co-director at Wisconsin's Institute for Enzyme Research, then MIT), each a deliberate move to a more prominent research platform, converging with two independent major scientific landmarks: the 1968 Nobel Prize for deciphering the genetic code, and the first total synthesis of a wholly artificial gene in 1970.

resourcefulness.rationale: Two independent documented instances decades apart: as a child in extreme material scarcity, walked door to door each morning seeking a household with an active cooking fire to obtain an ember for his own family's fire; and later self-funded his own further scientific training from savings rather than waiting for external funding to become available.

curiosity.rationale: Taught himself German specifically to access cutting-edge chemical literature not otherwise available to him, a single but concrete, self-initiated documented instance.

collaboration.rationale: Two independent documented instances: opened his own Nobel Prize lecture by explicitly crediting "a large number of workers professing a variety of scientific disciplines" rather than centering his individual role, and organized his research team to work in double shifts around the clock specifically to solve the genetic code, a sustained collective effort rather than solo work.

leadership_drive.rationale: Built and directed research programs at three successive institutions (University of British Columbia, co-director at Wisconsin, MIT), each requiring him to recruit, organize, and lead a functioning laboratory team, inferred as sustained leadership drive from this documented institutional pattern.

autonomy_need.rationale: Was specifically given, in a colleague's own words, "all the freedom in the world" to pursue his own research direction at the University of British Columbia and used it to build an independent program from a comparatively marginal institution, a single documented instance.
